expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 101 ('You are not allowed to perform this action'), from render_error_json(101) unless event_group.latest? in Api::EventGroupsController#update. The superseded event_groups row keeps its original title.
rationale: Writes to a superseded version fork the audit trail and can publish content the amendment already replaced; the latest? gate is the single point of defence.

title: QA_Platform_Publish against a non-existent event group uuid must not crash
preconditions: Authenticated purchaser; the referenced event group uuid does not resolve to any row in the caller's company.
steps: 1. POST /trade/template_input with an event_group_uuid that decodes to a non-existent id.
2. Assert a controlled 4xx and never a 500.
3. Assert no TradeRequest row is inserted.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 888 ('Invalid Parameters') from check_if_allowed_to_add_trade_to_event_group, which returns 888 when EventGroup.find_by(id: event_group_id, company_id: new_trade.company_id) is blank. No 5xx, no stage created.
rationale: The find_by is scoped by company_id, so this case doubles as a tenancy probe - a foreign uuid and a fake uuid must produce the same indistinguishable 888.

title: QA_Platform_Reject add-new-stage on an event that already contains an auction stage
preconditions: is_add_new_stage_allowed is TRUE. Event group {{eventGroupUuid}} holds an RFP stage {{tradeId}} plus a stage whose rfx_mode is auction or rfq_then_auction in a VALID_ADD_NEW_STAGE_STATUSES state.
steps: 1. Confirm the event group already contains an auction (or rfq_then_auction) stage.
2. POST /trade/template_input as an add-new-stage request referring to the RFP stage {{tradeId}}.
3. Assert the request is refused and the stage count is unchanged.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 1128 ('New stage cannot be added to an auction event') from AddNewStage::ValidateService#validate_auction_addition, which blocks when the collected rfx_modes include 'auction' or 'rfq_then_auction'.
rationale: Auctions carry live ranking state; appending a stage afterwards would invalidate every rank already broadcast to bidders and the savings baseline computed from it.

title: QA_Platform_Reject auction stage creation with a missing auction_config
preconditions: Draft event group {{eventGroupUuid}} exists with line items; no auction stage exists yet.
steps: 1. POST /trade/template_input with rfx_mode auction and no auction_config key at all.
2. Assert the request is refused with a numeric error code.
3. Assert no TradeRequest with rfx_mode auction and a null auction_config is persisted.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with a numeric error code (2 'Insufficient parameters' or 888 'Invalid Parameters'). No auction TradeRequest is created with auction_config null, since the enum {rank:0, price:1, rank_and_price:2, traffic_light:3, knockout:4, dutch:5, book_building:6} drives the whole bidding UI.
rationale: An auction row with a null auction_config renders an undefined bidding screen for vendors and makes get_ranking_key ambiguous - it must be impossible to create.

title: QA_Platform_Auction stage creation with an auction_config outside the enum
preconditions: Draft event group {{eventGroupUuid}} exists with line items.
steps: 1. POST /trade/template_input with rfx_mode auction and auction_config 'rank_and_price_and_rank'.
2. Assert the response is a controlled 4xx and never a 500.
3. Assert no auction stage is persisted for {{eventGroupUuid}}.
expectedResult: HTTP 4xx (422 with error code 2 or 888). No ArgumentError from the auction_config enum leaking as a 500; trade_requests row count unchanged.
rationale: 'rank_and_price' IS a real enum member, so a near-miss string is the realistic client bug - it must be caught as a validation failure rather than a crash.

title: QA_Platform_Create draft event group as the seed for an RFP-only project
preconditions: Authenticated purchaser with EventGroupPolicy#create? allowed in the workspace; {{productUuid}} and {{productQualityUuid}} resolve to an active Product / ProductQuality in the caller's company.
steps: 1. Authenticate as a purchaser of the workspace that owns {{productUuid}}.
2. POST /event_groups with status draft, a title and exactly one line item.
3. Assert HTTP 200 and that the response carries an event_group uuid plus one event_group_line_item id.
4. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} and confirm status is draft with no trade_requests yet.
expectedResult: HTTP 200. EventGroups::CreateService persists one EventGroup row with status=draft (enum 2) and one EventGroupLineItem with status=draft, serial_number=1 and meta_data.quantity={value:10,unitSymbol:'Nos'}; response is EventGroup::ShowSerializer.
rationale: Every RFx flavour starts from this one call; if the draft container or its line item does not persist correctly, every downstream stage, audience and bid assertion is testing on sand.

title: QA_Platform_Reject RFP stage creation when rfx_mode is sent in the wrong case
preconditions: A draft event group {{eventGroupUuid}} exists with at least one active line item and no stages yet.
steps: 1. POST /trade/template_input with rfx_mode 'RFP' (uppercase) against {{eventGroupUuid}}.
2. Assert the request is refused and no TradeRequest row is created for the event group.
3. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} and confirm the stage list is still empty.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with a numeric error code (2 insufficient parameters or 888 invalid parameters). TradeRequest#rfx_mode is an ActiveRecord enum {auction:0, rfq:1, rfq_then_auction:2, offline_trade:3, rfi:4, rfp:5} so 'RFP' is not a member; no trade_requests row must be inserted.
rationale: Rails enums are case sensitive and an unhandled ArgumentError on assignment is a 500 rather than a 422 - senior QA pins down which side of that line the API falls on.

title: QA_Platform_Reject RFP stage creation when event_group_uuid is blank
preconditions: Authenticated purchaser; no event group is referenced in the payload.
steps: 1. POST /trade/template_input with an empty event_group_uuid and rfx_mode rfp.
2. Assert HTTP 422 and a numeric error code in the body.
3. Assert no orphan TradeRequest row is created with a null event_group_id.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 888 ('Invalid Parameters') from check_if_allowed_to_add_trade_to_event_group, which returns 888 when EventGroup.find_by(id:, company_id:) is blank. No TradeRequest is persisted.
rationale: An orphan stage with no event_group_id silently corrupts every dashboard and history query that joins through event_groups; the guard must fire before any write.

title: QA_Platform_Reject a third stage on an event that already has both RFP and RFQ
preconditions: Event group {{eventGroupUuid}} has exactly two TradeRequests in VALID_ADD_NEW_STAGE_STATUSES (active/closed/requested/draft): one rfp and one rfq. The is_add_new_stage_allowed config is TRUE for the company. {{tradeId}} is the RFP stage.
steps: 1. Confirm the event group holds exactly one rfp stage and one rfq stage.
2. POST /trade/template_input as an add-new-stage request referring to the RFP stage {{tradeId}}.
3. Assert the request is refused and no third TradeRequest is created.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 1129 ('New stage cannot be added to an RFP and RFQ event') from AddNewStage::ValidateService#validate_rfp_rfq_addition, which fires when trade_requests.size == 2 and the rfx_modes set is exactly {rfp, rfq}. No third stage row is written.
rationale: The RFP-plus-RFQ shape is the terminal state of the two-stage funnel; letting a third stage in would break stage ordering, award mapping and the vendor-facing timeline.

title: QA_Platform_Reject add-new-stage when the referring stage is an RFQ not an RFP
preconditions: is_add_new_stage_allowed is TRUE for the company. {{tradeId}} is a TradeRequest with rfx_mode rfq belonging to {{eventGroupUuid}}.
steps: 1. Pick the RFQ stage {{tradeId}} of event group {{eventGroupUuid}}.
2. POST /trade/template_input as an add-new-stage request referring to that RFQ stage.
3. Assert the request is refused with the RFP-origin error, not a generic parameter error.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 2001 ('New stage cannot be added unless the referring stage is an RFP'), from AddNewStage::ValidateService#validate_referring_trade_is_rfp which requires @trade_request.is_rfi_or_rfp?. No new TradeRequest is created.
rationale: spec/services/add_new_stage/validate_service_spec.rb pins 2001 for both RFQ and auction origins; regressing this would let buyers bolt stages onto commercial rounds after bids exist.

title: QA_Platform_Feature-flag error takes precedence over the RFP-origin error on add-new-stage
preconditions: CustomConfiguration is_add_new_stage_allowed is FALSE (or absent) for the company owning {{eventGroupUuid}}, AND the referring stage {{tradeId}} is an RFQ - so two distinct guards would both fail.
steps: 1. Turn the is_add_new_stage_allowed config off for the company.
2. POST /trade/template_input as an add-new-stage request referring to the RFQ stage {{tradeId}}.
3. Assert the returned numeric code is the feature-flag one, proving guard ordering.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 1127 ('Adding a new stage to a live event is not enabled for this company') and specifically NOT 2001, because validate_feature_enabled runs first in AddNewStage::ValidateService#validate.
rationale: Guard ordering is asserted directly in validate_service_spec.rb; a reorder would leak the existence of stage rules to companies that never bought the feature and give support the wrong message.

title: QA_Platform_Create draft event group as the seed for an RFQ-only event
preconditions: Authenticated purchaser with create rights; {{productUuid}} and {{productQualityUuid}} are active in the caller's workspace.
steps: 1. POST /event_groups with status draft and one line item quantity 10 Nos.
2. Assert HTTP 200 and capture the returned event group uuid.
3. GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}}/get_line_items and assert exactly one active/draft line item is returned.
expectedResult: HTTP 200; EventGroup created with status draft and precomputed_data.creator_fields.creator_quantity populated so EventGroupLineItem#quantity returns 10.0 and #unit_symbol returns 'Nos'.
rationale: RFQ-only is the highest-volume event type in production; the quantity/unit round-trip through precomputed_data is the exact field bids are later validated against.

title: QA_Platform_Reject a second RFQ stage of the same rfx_mode on a published event
preconditions: Event group {{eventGroupUuid}} is published (active) and already owns one TradeRequest with rfx_mode rfq in status active/closed/scheduled/draft.
steps: 1. Publish an RFQ stage on {{eventGroupUuid}} and let it reach active.
2. POST /trade/template_input again with rfx_mode rfq and stage_no 2 for the same event group.
3. Assert the duplicate is refused and the event group still has exactly one RFQ stage.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 830 ('Same type of event already exists for this Project.') raised by check_if_allowed_to_add_trade_to_event_group when old_tr_with_same_rfx_mode is present and is_new_stage_addition is false. No second RFQ TradeRequest is inserted.
rationale: A duplicate commercial stage splits bids across two trade_requests and makes latest_commercial_stage ambiguous - the 830 guard is the only thing stopping a double-award.

title: QA_Platform_SQL injection payload in rfx_mode on RFQ stage creation
preconditions: Draft event group {{eventGroupUuid}} exists; a baseline count of trade_requests rows is recorded.
steps: 1. POST /trade/template_input with rfx_mode set to a SQL injection string.
2. Assert the response is a controlled 4xx, never a 500 and never a raw ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid message.
3. Re-query GET /event_groups/{{eventGroupUuid}} and confirm the event group and its stages are untouched.
expectedResult: HTTP 4xx (422 expected) with a numeric error code; no 5xx, no SQL fragment or backtrace echoed. trade_requests table still exists and its row count is unchanged.
rationale: rfx_mode is fed straight into TradeRequest.where(...) and pluck comparisons in check_if_allowed_to_add_trade_to_event_group; a senior QA proves the enum layer sanitises before the query builder ever sees it.

title: QA_Platform_Template response for a non-existent trade must return a numeric error not a partial template
preconditions: Authenticated purchaser; {{tradeId}} is substituted with an id that has no trade_requests row.
steps: 1. GET /trade/{{tradeId}}?response_type=template for a non-existent trade id.
2. Assert a controlled 4xx with a numeric error code and never a 500.
3. Assert the body contains no template schema, no tab definitions and no vendor data.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with a numeric error code such as 95 ('Trade Request not found') or 101 ('You are not allowed to perform this action'). Api::TradeController#show does TradeRequest.where(id:).last and then calls trade_request.is_allowed_to_view?(Current.user), so a nil trade must be caught before that dereference.
rationale: The template response drives the entire buyer form; a half-rendered template on a missing trade both 500s and leaks the shape of the schema builder.

title: QA_Platform_Stage creation with the template_name query parameter removed
preconditions: Draft event group {{eventGroupUuid}} exists with line items. The request is sent to the template_input action but the template_name query parameter is dropped by the client.
steps: 1. POST to the template_input path with template_name empty and additional_fields still present.
2. Assert the response is a controlled 4xx and never a 500.
3. Assert no TradeRequest is created against an unresolved template.
expectedResult: No 5xx. Expected HTTP 422 with a numeric error code (2 or 888). transform_trade_product and transform_config both run off the resolved template, so a blank template_name must be refused before a TradeRequest is written with a null template reference.
rationale: template_name is a query parameter rather than a body field, so it is the first thing lost by a proxy rewrite or a badly-built URL - the server must not assume it is present.

title: QA_Platform_Orders listing must not leak other tenants rows via a forged company filter
preconditions: Authenticated as a purchaser of company A. A company B exists with its own awarded orders. The listing is expected to be scoped by Current.allowed_companies.
steps: 1. GET /orders as company A with no filters and record the returned order ids.
2. GET /orders again appending a forged company/vendor filter that names company B and {{vendorUuid}}.
3. Assert the second response is a subset of the first and contains zero rows belonging to company B.
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with results strictly scoped to Current.allowed_companies, or HTTP 422 with error code 455 / 101. Under no circumstances may a client-supplied company or vendor filter widen the result set beyond the caller's own tenancy.
rationale: Listing endpoints take filters straight from params and merge them into the scope; a filter that widens rather than narrows is the most common tenancy leak in list APIs and orders carry final awarded prices.

title: QA_Platform_Reject an rfx_mode that is not a member of the TradeRequest enum
preconditions: Draft event group {{eventGroupUuid}} exists with line items and no stages.
steps: 1. POST /trade/template_input with rfx_mode 'rfx'.
2. Assert HTTP 422 with a numeric error code.
3. Assert no TradeRequest is created for {{eventGroupUuid}}.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with a numeric error code (2 or 888). Valid rfx_mode members are exactly auction, rfq, rfq_then_auction, offline_trade, rfi and rfp; 'rfx' must be refused before any row is written.
rationale: 'rfx' is the product's own umbrella word, so it is the most likely string a client or an integration will send by mistake - it must not slip past the enum.

title: QA_Platform_Reject stage creation with a null rfx_mode
preconditions: Draft event group {{eventGroupUuid}} exists with line items.
steps: 1. POST /trade/template_input with rfx_mode explicitly null.
2. Assert HTTP 422 with a numeric error code.
3. Assert no TradeRequest with a null rfx_mode exists for the event group.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 2 ('Insufficient parameters') or 888. A null rfx_mode would make check_if_allowed_to_add_trade_to_event_group compare nil.to_s against existing modes and would break EventGroup#latest_commercial_stage which filters on rfx_mode.
rationale: Null enums are silently allowed by ActiveRecord unless explicitly validated, and a null rfx_mode row poisons every stage-type scope in the model.

title: QA_Platform_Numeric rfx_mode ordinal must not bypass the string enum contract
preconditions: Draft event group {{eventGroupUuid}} exists with line items.
steps: 1. POST /trade/template_input with rfx_mode sent as the integer 5 (the underlying ordinal for rfp).
2. Assert the response is a controlled 4xx or, if accepted, that the stored rfx_mode is exactly 'rfp'.
3. Assert no row is stored with an rfx_mode the API contract does not document.
expectedResult: No 5xx. Rails enums accept the integer ordinal, so 5 may map to rfp; the check_if_allowed_to_add_trade_to_event_group duplicate check compares trade_request.rfx_mode.to_s against params rfx_mode.to_s ('5' vs 'rfp'), so an integer would BYPASS the 830 duplicate-stage guard. Assert either rejection or correct duplicate detection.
rationale: The duplicate-stage guard does a string comparison against the enum name; sending the ordinal is a real bypass of error 830 and would let a second RFQ stage through.

title: QA_Platform_Reject version creation for an item_type outside the allow-list
preconditions: Authenticated purchaser. Api::ItemVersionsController::ALLOWED_ITEM_TYPES is exactly ['EventGroup'].
steps: 1. POST /item_versions with item_type 'TradeRequest'.
2. Assert HTTP 422 with a numeric error code.
3. Assert no item_versions row is created and no class other than EventGroup is constantized.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 2 ('Insufficient parameters'), from the guard that fires when item_type is blank, item_id is blank, or ALLOWED_ITEM_TYPES excludes item_type. The subsequent item_type.constantize must never run.
rationale: item_type is passed to constantize; the allow-list is the only thing between a user-supplied string and arbitrary class resolution, so it must be verified as a hard deny rather than a soft filter.

title: QA_Platform_Reject creating a version of a draft event group
preconditions: Event group {{eventGroupUuid}} exists in status draft (never published) and is the latest version.
steps: 1. Create a draft event group and do not publish any stage.
2. POST /item_versions with item_type EventGroup and the draft event group's id.
3. Assert the request is refused and no new event group replica is created.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error code 888 ('Invalid Parameters'), from render_error_json(888) when item.blank? || !item.active? || !item.latest? - a draft EventGroup fails active? (status enum draft = 2, active = 1). No item_versions row and no replica EventGroup are created.
rationale: Versioning a draft would branch an event that was never published to vendors, producing two 'latest' candidates and breaking every latest? guard used across update, publish and move_to_auction.

title: QA_Platform_Version creation with a missing item_id and a hostile item_id type
preconditions: Authenticated purchaser. Run twice: once with item_id omitted, once with item_id sent as an array.
steps: 1. POST /item_versions with item_type EventGroup and no item_id at all and assert HTTP 422.
2. POST /item_versions with item_id sent as an array of ids.
3. Assert both calls return a controlled 4xx and never a 500, and that no item_versions row is created.
expectedResult: No 5xx. The omitted-id variant returns HTTP 422 with error code 2 ('Insufficient parameters'). The array variant must return 422 with code 2 or 888 - EventGroup.find_by(id: [array]) would otherwise resolve the FIRST element and version an event the caller never named.
rationale: An array where a scalar is expected is the standard Rails mass-assignment trick; find_by silently accepts it, so this is a real authorization-bypass shape and not just a type nit.

title: QA_Platform_payment_proof_rejects_empty_payload
preconditions: a caller on the client admin dashboard (vendor_payments#submit_proof is whitelisted only for client_admin_dashboard)
steps: 1. POST /vendor_payments/submit_proof with an empty body.
2. Assert refusal and that no VendorPayment row is created.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 845; VendorPayments::SubmissionForm validates presence of event_id, vendor_id, paid_amount and proof_document_url, so the form is invalid and VendorPayments::SubmitProofService never runs.
rationale: This endpoint records that money was paid to a vendor; an empty payload must never create a payment stub that later reconciles against a real invoice.

title: QA_Platform_payment_proof_rejects_missing_proof_document
preconditions: a caller on the client admin dashboard
steps: 1. POST /vendor_payments/submit_proof with event, vendor and paid_amount but no proof_document_url.
2. Assert refusal - a payment cannot be recorded without its proof.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 845 (proof_document_url presence validation fails inside SubmissionForm#payment_confirmation=); no VendorPayment is saved.
rationale: Proof of payment is the audit artefact for bid-fee reconciliation; presence must be enforced server-side, not just by the upload widget.

title: QA_Platform_payment_proof_rejects_negative_paid_amount
preconditions: a caller on the client admin dashboard
steps: 1. POST /vendor_payments/submit_proof with paid_amount set to a negative number.
2. Assert refusal on the numericality rule.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 845; `validates :paid_amount, numericality: { greater_than_or_equal_to: 0.0 }` fails, so no VendorPayment row and no bid-fee credit is created.
rationale: A negative payment would credit the vendor's bid fee in reverse; boundary values on money fields are non-negotiable coverage.

title: QA_Platform_payment_proof_rejects_unknown_event_and_vendor
preconditions: a caller on the client admin dashboard
steps: 1. POST /vendor_payments/submit_proof with fabricated event_id and vendor_id values.
2. Assert refusal from the existence validators.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 845; event_must_exist (EventGroup.active.find_by) and vendor_must_exist (Company.active.find_by) both add :not_found errors, so PaymentFactory is never called.
rationale: Payments must be anchored to a real event and a real vendor company; an unresolvable pair reaching the factory would create an unattributable payment record.

title: QA_Platform_payment_proof_survives_hostile_amount_and_url
preconditions: a caller on the client admin dashboard
steps: 1. POST /vendor_payments/submit_proof with a non-numeric paid_amount, a SQL fragment in event_id and a javascript: proof URL.
2. Assert a clean 422 with no stack trace and nothing persisted.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 845 and no 5xx: the numericality validator rejects the non-numeric amount, ActiveRecord casts the injected event_id to an integer so no SQL is interpolated, and ParamsAuth#sanitize_input_params has already stripped the script tag from remark.
rationale: Hostile input on the payment surface must fail as validation, not as an exception or an accepted record; this also documents that proof_document_url has no scheme validation today.

title: QA_Platform_payment_proof_requires_session
preconditions: no session token
steps: 1. POST /vendor_payments/submit_proof with a complete-looking payload and no session token.
2. Assert an authentication failure before the form is built.
expectedResult: Refused by the ApiAuth filter chain: HTTP 422 error.code 2 when no access token is present, or api_error_auth_failed when login is required for vendor_payments#submit_proof in app_auth_config; Current.user is never merged into submission_params and no VendorPayment is created.
rationale: submit_proof stamps Current.user as the payer of record; an unauthenticated call must be impossible or the payment audit trail loses its actor.

title: QA_Platform_approvals_read_for_visible_intake
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake read_record permission and can see {{intakeId}}
steps: 1. GET /intake_requests/{{intakeId}}/approvals.
2. Assert HTTP 200 and that approval requests are returned newest-first with per-request edit permissions.
expectedResult: HTTP 200, array serialised by ApprovalWorkflow::IntakeApprovalSerializer sorted by created_at desc, including is_user_allowed_to_force_resolve_pending_steps; read-only.
rationale: Approvals drive who can release spend; the force-resolve flag in this payload is a privilege signal the UI trusts, so its presence and value must be verified.

title: QA_Platform_approvals_rejects_unknown_intake_id
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake read_record permission
steps: 1. GET /intake_requests/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}/approvals using a non-existent identifier.
2. Assert a not-found style refusal rather than an empty 200.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 706 (Intake request not found) from the verify_request_exists before_action; ParamsAuth#check_for_uuid decodes the non-numeric id to nil first.
rationale: Distinguishing not-found (706) from not-authorized (455) is what stops the endpoint being used to enumerate intake ids across tenants.

title: QA_Platform_approval_flows_rejects_non_draft_intake
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake create_record permission, and {{intakeId}} is an intake that is already active or completed (not draft and not rejected)
steps: 1. GET /intake_requests/{{intakeId}}/approval_flows for an already-published intake.
2. Assert refusal, since approval flows may only be resolved for draft or rejected intakes.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 101 (You are not allowed to perform this action) because the draft_scope in #applicable_approval_flows filters status to [:draft, :rejected] and returns nil.
rationale: Re-resolving the approval chain on a live intake would let a requester swap approvers mid-flight; the draft-only scope is the control and must be pinned by a test.

title: QA_Platform_publish_rejects_undecodable_intake_id
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake create_record permission
steps: 1. PATCH /intake_requests/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}/publish with an approval_flow_id and remark.
2. Assert the refusal happens before WorkflowRuns::CreateService is invoked.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2 (blank id after uuid decode); status is never set to :active and no workflow run is created.
rationale: Publish is the point of no return for an intake; the negative path must be proven to short-circuit before the transaction and the workflow kick-off.

title: QA_Platform_publish_requires_authenticated_session
preconditions: no session token
steps: 1. PATCH /intake_requests/{{intakeId}}/publish with no session/access token headers.
2. Assert an authentication failure and that the intake remains in draft.
expectedResult: Refused by ApiAuth before the controller action: HTTP 422 error.code 2 when the access token is absent, or api_error_auth_failed when the app token resolves but no user session exists. IntakeRequest.status is unchanged and no approval workflow is started.
rationale: An unauthenticated publish would push spend into the approval chain; auth must be enforced by the filter chain, not by the action body.

title: QA_Platform_withdraw_rejects_draft_intake
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake update_record permission, and {{intakeId}} is a DRAFT intake request (never published)
steps: 1. POST /intake_requests/{{intakeId}}/withdraw_request for a draft intake.
2. Assert refusal with the withdraw-not-allowed code and no workflow-run mutation.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 707 (Can't withdraw Intake request) because status must be in ['active','to_be_completed']; no approval request is withdrawn.
rationale: Illegal state transitions on withdraw would strand workflow_run_steps in a running state with no parent request; the status whitelist is the guard.

title: QA_Platform_withdraw_rejects_unknown_intake
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake update_record permission
steps: 1. POST /intake_requests/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}/withdraw_request.
2. Assert the authorization-scoped refusal.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 455 (You are not authorized to perform this action); IntakeRequest.for_user(..., action: WITHDRAW, company: Current.workspace).find_by returns nil.
rationale: for_user is the tenant + access-list filter for withdraw; asserting 455 on an unknown id proves the scope is applied before any state check.

title: QA_Platform_issue_request_rejects_attachments_without_remark
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake update_record permission, and {{intakeId}} is an intake request that is NOT in the to_be_completed state
steps: 1. POST /intake_requests/{{intakeId}}/issue_request with an attachments array but no remark.
2. Assert the intake is not marked completed and no closing remark row is created.
expectedResult: HTTP 422: error.code 4 (Failed to issue intake request) from the !to_be_completed? guard, or error.code 15 from create_closing_remark when remark is blank. IntakeRequest.status stays unchanged and no ExpressionEvaluator record is written.
rationale: Closing an intake is terminal; an attachment alone must never be treated as a valid closure, and the state guard must be evaluated before the remark payload.

title: QA_Platform_issue_request_handles_malformed_attachments_shape
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake update_record permission, and {{intakeId}} is an intake request that is NOT in the to_be_completed state
steps: 1. POST /intake_requests/{{intakeId}}/issue_request sending attachments as an object instead of the expected array of strings, with remark omitted.
2. Assert a clean 4xx rather than a Sorbet/NoMethodError 500.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 (error.code 4 or 15) and no 500. create_closing_remark is typed T.nilable(T::Array[String]) for attachments, so a Hash must be refused by the blank-remark guard before the signature is exercised.
rationale: The attachments parameter crosses a sig-typed boundary; a client sending the wrong shape must get a validation error, not a type error leaking a stack trace.

title: QA_Platform_share_rejects_invalid_access_type
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake read_record permission and can see {{intakeId}}
steps: 1. PATCH /intake_requests/{{intakeId}}/share with shared_with[0].access_type set to a privilege above viewer.
2. Assert refusal and that no AccessList row is created for {{userUuid}}.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2 from AccessLists::ValidateService#valid_access_types?, because IntakeRequest::SHAREABLE_ACCESS_TYPES is ['viewer'] only; ShareService never runs and no access grant is persisted.
rationale: Intake attachments contain quotes and pricing; an access_type that escalates past viewer would silently widen document visibility, and the whitelist is the only guard.

title: QA_Platform_run_steps_read_returns_workflow_documents
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake read_record permission and can see {{intakeId}}
steps: 1. GET /intake_requests/{{intakeId}}/run_steps.
2. Assert HTTP 200 with the run-step and approval-request payload serialised by Intake::IntakeRunStepsSerializer.
expectedResult: HTTP 200; read-only path that eager-loads forms, form_pages, form_page_responses and access_lists. Unauthorised callers would instead get 422 error.code 455.
rationale: This is the timeline the buyer sees for attachments and approvals; it is also the heaviest eager-load in the intake controller, so it is worth a standing smoke assertion.

title: QA_Platform_intake_create_rejects_missing_title
preconditions: a caller whose role is member or manager, holding the intake create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /intake_requests with template_item_mapping_id and forms populated but the title key omitted entirely.
2. Assert the response is refused and that no draft IntakeRequest row is created.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 (Insufficient parameters) from the params[:title].blank? guard at the top of Api::IntakeRequestsController#create; no IntakeRequest, Form or IntakeProduct row is inserted.
rationale: The three-way blank guard is the only thing standing between a malformed client payload and a half-built intake; a regression here creates orphan drafts that later block PR creation.

title: QA_Platform_intake_create_rejects_missing_forms
preconditions: a caller whose role is member or manager, holding the intake create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /intake_requests with a valid title and template_item_mapping_id but no forms array.
2. Assert refusal before build_forms runs.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2; the forms.blank? branch fires before the ActiveRecord transaction opens, so nothing is written.
rationale: An intake with no forms cannot be validated, approved or converted to a PR; it must be refused at the boundary rather than at publish time.

title: QA_Platform_intake_create_survives_injection_payload_in_title
preconditions: a caller whose role is member or manager, holding the intake create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /intake_requests with a script tag and a SQL fragment inside title and no forms key.
2. Assert the API refuses the call and never echoes the raw script tag back.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2 (forms missing). ParamsAuth#sanitize_input_params has already stripped the HTML via strip_html_tags_except_mentions, so no raw <script> is stored or reflected and no 5xx is raised.
rationale: Titles are rendered in the buyer dashboard and in approval e-mails; the global sanitizer is the single control point and needs an explicit regression test.

title: QA_Platform_intake_configs_and_currency_read
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake create_record permission (IntakeRequestPolicy#configs? maps to create?)
steps: 1. GET /intake_requests/configs.
2. Assert HTTP 200 and a currency_config object for the caller's workspace.
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with a currency_config payload from Current.workspace.get_currency_config; read-only, no DB writes.
rationale: Every intake form is priced off this config; if it 403s or returns an empty currency the whole intake creation screen breaks before a single request is raised.

title: QA_Platform_intake_draft_read_is_scoped_to_caller
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake create_record permission and has at most one draft intake in the current workspace
steps: 1. GET /intake_requests/draft.
2. Assert HTTP 200 and that the returned draft (if any) belongs to the calling user and the current workspace only.
expectedResult: HTTP 200 returning the last IntakeRequest.draft scoped by user: Current.user AND company: Current.workspace, or {success:true} when none exists; never another user's draft.
rationale: The draft endpoint returns an in-progress request with prices and vendor details; the user+company scoping is the tenant boundary and must be asserted, not assumed.

title: QA_Platform_pr_retry_rejects_intake_not_in_pr_failed
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake update_record permission, and {{intakeId}} is an intake whose pr_status is NOT pr_failed
steps: 1. POST /intake_requests/{{intakeId}}/purchase_request.
2. Assert refusal and that IntakeToPrWorker is not enqueued.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 101 from the !intake_request.pr_failed? guard; no Sidekiq job is pushed and no PurchaseRequest is created.
rationale: PR creation is the money-side handoff; retrying a non-failed intake would double-create purchase requests, so the state gate is the highest-value assertion in this flow.

title: QA_Platform_pr_retry_rejects_unknown_intake_and_is_workspace_scoped
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake update_record permission
steps: 1. POST /intake_requests/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}/purchase_request.
2. Assert 455 and confirm no worker is enqueued.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 455 because IntakeRequest.for_user(...).find_by(id: nil) is nil.
rationale: This action calls for_user WITHOUT company: Current.workspace, unlike every sibling action in the controller; that asymmetry makes the id-resolution path worth explicit regression coverage.

title: QA_Platform_intake_update_rejects_unknown_id_on_patch
preconditions: a caller who holds the intake update_record permission
steps: 1. PATCH /intake_requests/QA_Platform_{{stamp}} with a forms payload.
2. Assert the not-found refusal from the before_action, before update_intake_request runs.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 706 (Intake request not found) from verify_request_exists, which excludes in_active records; nothing is written.
rationale: The update action can rewrite forms, products and approval routing, so the id guard must fire in the filter chain rather than deep inside the helper.

title: Create L1 category with name + hierarchy_type
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission; Current.workspace resolved
steps: 1. Authenticate and resolve workspace
2. POST /product_categories with name QA_Platform_Cat_{{stamp}} and hierarchy_type category
3. Read the ProductCategorySerializer response and capture the returned uuid
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with ProductCategorySerializer payload. New product_categories row: name=QA_Platform_Cat_{{stamp}}, hierarchy_type=0 (category), status=1 (active, forced by build_product_category), company_id=Current.workspace.id, ancestry=NULL.
rationale: The single happy path that every other master-data case depends on; it pins the two truly mandatory fields and proves status is force-set to active rather than defaulting to in_active.

title: Reject category create when name key is absent
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /product_categories sending only hierarchy_type
2. Assert the app error code and HTTP status
3. Assert no product_categories row was inserted
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 and message 'Insufficient parameters' from the name.blank? || hierarchy_type.blank? guard. No DB write.
rationale: Guards the explicit blank check in the controller; a regression here would push a nameless record down to ProductCategory#name_present and change the error contract the dashboard parses.

title: Reject category create when name is an empty string
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with name set to empty string
2. Assert HTTP 422 and error code 2
3. Assert product_categories count is unchanged
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. No row created; the ProductCategory#name_present validator is never reached.
rationale: Empty string and missing key are different client behaviours; both must land on the same 422/code 2 contract or the dashboard shows a generic 500 toast.

title: Reject category create when name is whitespace only
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with name set to three spaces
2. Assert HTTP 422 and error code 2
3. Confirm no whitespace-named category exists for the workspace
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2. Rails blank? treats a whitespace-only string as blank, so the controller guard fires and nothing is persisted.
rationale: Whitespace-only names are the classic way junk master data leaks into pickers; this proves blank? (not empty?) is what the controller relies on.

title: Reject category create when hierarchy_type is missing
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with only a name
2. Assert HTTP 422 and error code 2
3. Assert nothing was written
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. No row created; hierarchy_type is guarded only at the controller level, so this guard is the only thing preventing a NULL hierarchy_type row.
rationale: hierarchy_type has no model-level presence validation, so this controller guard is the single line of defence against categories that no hierarchy scope can ever find.

title: Invalid hierarchy_type enum value must not 500
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with hierarchy_type set to supercategory
2. Assert the HTTP status is below 500
3. Assert the response body is JSON, not an HTML error page
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. build_product_category calls ProductCategory.new(hierarchy_type: 'supercategory') and the enum {category:0, family:1, commodity:2} raises ArgumentError with no rescue_from in ApplicationController, so an unhandled 500 is the likely real behaviour and is a defect. Acceptable outcome is 422 with a JSON error body.
rationale: Rails enum assignment raises ArgumentError rather than adding a validation error; with only Pundit::NotAuthorizedError rescued, a typo'd enum from any client becomes a 500.

title: Wrong-case hierarchy_type CATEGORY must not 500
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with hierarchy_type set to uppercase CATEGORY
2. Assert status below 500 and a JSON body
3. Assert no row with a NULL hierarchy_type was created
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. Rails enums are case-sensitive, so 'CATEGORY' is not a member of {category, family, commodity} and hits the same ArgumentError path. Expected safe behaviour is 422 with a JSON error.
rationale: Integration partners and bulk importers routinely send upper-cased enums; case sensitivity must degrade to a 422, never a crash.

title: Reject category create when gst is outside 0-100
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with gst 150.5
2. Assert HTTP 422 and error code 865
3. Repeat with gst -1 and expect the identical code
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 865 and message 'GST must be a value between 0 and 100', raised by invalid_gst? before any record is built. No DB write.
rationale: invalid_gst? runs before the blank-name guard, so it is the earliest exit in the action; a wrong GST silently persisted would corrupt every downstream tax computation.

title: SQL injection payload in category name must not execute
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission; note existing category count
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with a name containing a DROP TABLE payload
2. Assert status below 500 and a JSON body
3. Re-query GET /product_categories and confirm the table still responds and prior categories are intact
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx and must not execute SQL. ActiveRecord binds the insert, so the payload is stored as a literal string. product_categories must still exist and subsequent reads must succeed.
rationale: ProductCategory has raw-SQL scopes (search_from_query interpolates the query, search_relevant_product_category builds Arel.sql) so injection surface genuinely exists in this model.

title: XSS payload in category name is stripped by param sanitizer
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with a script tag embedded in the name
2. Assert status below 500
3. Read the returned name and assert it contains no script markup
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. ParamsAuth#sanitize_input_params runs strip_html_tags_except_mentions on every string param before the action, so the persisted and echoed name must have the script tags removed.
rationale: The sanitizer is a global before_action; if the route is ever added to ROUTES_TO_SKIP_HTML_STRIPPING, stored XSS reaches every category dropdown in the dashboard.

title: Create buyer hub with city_uuid and location_type
preconditions: A city whose state has a zone exists and its uuid is bound to {{cityUuid}}; user has buyer_hub create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /buyer_hubs/create with name, city_uuid, location_type and location_code
2. Assert HTTP 200 and the rendered app_buyer_hub partial
3. Assert the hub is returned by GET /buyer_hubs/all
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with the buyer_hub partial. New buyer_hubs row: status=1 (active, hard-set), city_id decoded from {{cityUuid}}, company_id=Current.workspace.id, location_type=0, and zone_id back-filled from City.find_by_id(city_id).state.zone_id.
rationale: The zone_id is derived server-side from the city's state, not sent by the client; this is the only case that proves that derivation actually populates.

title: Missing city_uuid must not 500
preconditions: User has buyer_hub create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /buyer_hubs/create with a name and location_type but no city_uuid
2. Assert the status is below 500 and the body is JSON
3. Assert no buyer_hubs row was created
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. The first statement after reading params is City.find_by_id(city_id).state&.zone_id with no nil guard on the City lookup, so a nil city_id raises NoMethodError and produces an unhandled 500 - a real defect. Correct behaviour is HTTP 422.
rationale: This is a concrete unguarded nil dereference in Api::BuyerHubsController#create; safe navigation is applied to .state but not to the find_by_id result, so the most common client mistake crashes the endpoint.

title: Non-existent city_uuid must not 500
preconditions: User has buyer_hub create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /buyer_hubs/create with a decodable but unknown city uuid
2. Assert status below 500 and a JSON error body
3. Assert no hub was persisted
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. City.find_by_id returns nil for the decoded id and the same unguarded .state call raises NoMethodError. Acceptable behaviour is HTTP 422 with a JSON error and no DB write.
rationale: Separates the 'param absent' case from the 'param present but dangling' case - both hit the same defect but a fix could easily address only one.

title: Reject buyer hub create when name is blank
preconditions: A valid city with a zone exists and its uuid is bound to {{cityUuid}}
steps: 1. POST /buyer_hubs/create with an empty name and a valid city_uuid
2. Assert HTTP 422 and error code 15
3. Assert no buyer_hubs row was created
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 15 'Operation failed' and a detail array containing "Name can't be blank" from BuyerHub validates :name, presence: true.
rationale: buyer_hubs.name is NOT NULL at the DB level too, so an app-level validation bypass would turn a clean 422 into a PG NotNullViolation 500.

title: Reject duplicate location_code for the same company
preconditions: An active hub with location_code QA_Platform_DupLoc already exists in the workspace
steps: 1. Create a hub with location_code QA_Platform_DupLoc
2. POST /buyer_hubs/create again with the same location_code and a different name
3. Assert HTTP 422 and that only one active hub holds the code
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 15 and the location_code taken_already message from BuyerHub#duplicate_location_code. The validator is conditional on location_code.present? && self.active?, and the controller always sets status: :active on create.
rationale: location_code is the natural key ERP and delivery integrations join on; because uniqueness is scoped to active hubs only, deactivating a hub silently frees the code.

title: Invalid location_type enum must not 500
preconditions: A valid city with a zone exists and its uuid is bound to {{cityUuid}}
steps: 1. POST /buyer_hubs/create with location_type set to warehouse_center
2. Assert status below 500 and a JSON body
3. Assert no hub was created
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. BuyerHub.new(location_type: 'warehouse_center') is called with the enum {delivery_center:0, buying_team_hub:1, zonal_head_office:2, retail_store:3, other:4, free_text:5}; an unknown member raises ArgumentError which the action does not rescue.
rationale: location_type is set directly in BuyerHub.new rather than by a guarded assignment, so it is the enum most exposed to raw client input on this endpoint.

title: Create product under a family with product_code and one variant
preconditions: An active family category exists and its uuid is bound to {{familyUuid}}; user has product create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /products with name, category_uuid {{familyUuid}}, product_code and a single variant
2. Assert HTTP 201
3. Assert the serialized product carries the category and one product_quality
expectedResult: HTTP 201 created with {product, approval_workflows}. Products::CreateService persists status=1 (active), category_id decoded from {{familyUuid}}, and Product#build_product_quality creates one active product_qualities row.
rationale: Products are the leaf of the whole master-data chain; this single case proves uuid decode, category linkage, variant nesting and the approval branch all wire up together.

title: Reject product create when name is missing
preconditions: An active family exists and its uuid is bound to {{familyUuid}}
steps: 1. POST /products with category_uuid and product_code but no name
2. Assert HTTP 422
3. Assert Product count is unchanged
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 8 'Model error' and a detail message containing "Name can't be blank", produced by validates :name, presence: true. No products row inserted.
rationale: name is the only unconditional presence validation on Product; its error must arrive as code 8 with the model sentence, because the dashboard renders that sentence verbatim.

title: Reject product create when category_uuid is absent
preconditions: User has product create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /products with a name and product_code but no category_uuid
2. Assert HTTP 422
3. Assert no product row was created
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 8 and a message from Product#category_presence stating the category is blank. Note belongs_to :category is declared optional: true, so this custom validator is the only guard.
rationale: belongs_to :category is optional at the association level, so removing category_presence would let category-less products through and break every category-scoped report.

title: Reject product create when category_uuid points to a non-existent category
preconditions: User has product create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /products with a syntactically valid but unknown category uuid
2. Assert HTTP 422
3. Assert no product row references the bogus id
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 8. check_for_uuid decodes category_uuid to a category_id that matches no row, Product#category is nil and category_presence adds the blank-category error. No dangling category_id persisted.
rationale: Product.category_id has no DB foreign key (only an index), so the app-level category_presence check is the sole thing preventing dangling references.

title: Reject duplicate product_code within the same company
preconditions: A product with product_code QA_Platform_DupCode already exists in the workspace; allow_duplicate_product_code config is off
steps: 1. Create a product with product_code QA_Platform_DupCode
2. POST /products again with the same product_code and a different name
3. Assert HTTP 422 and that only one product carries that code
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 8 and the product_code taken_already message from Product#duplicate_product_code. The conflict scope is Product.where(status: [:active, :draft, :in_review, :rejected]), so an in_active twin would NOT trigger it.
rationale: Article/product code uniqueness is the field ERP integrations key on; the status filter means soft-deleted products free up their code, and that nuance must be verified not assumed.

title: Blank product_code when article code is mandatory
preconditions: Workspace has article_code_mandatory_on_product_create? enabled; family uuid bound to {{familyUuid}}
steps: 1. POST /products with an empty-string product_code
2. Assert HTTP 422 and the exact error code
3. Assert Product count did not change
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 1120 and message 'Article Code is required'. The controller guard uses params['product_code'].to_s.strip.blank?, so empty string, nil and whitespace all take this branch before the transaction opens. If the config is off, the same call is accepted with a NULL product_code.
rationale: This exact behaviour is pinned in spec/controllers/api/products_controller_spec.rb; the API suite must assert the same 1120 contract so a config or copy change is caught outside RSpec too.

title: Invalid product_type enum must not 500
preconditions: Family uuid bound to {{familyUuid}}; user has product create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /products with product_type set to a value outside the enum
2. Assert the status is below 500 and the body is JSON
3. Assert no product row was created with a NULL product_type
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. Products::CreateService assigns product.product_type directly; an unknown enum member raises ArgumentError. The action only rescues ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, so a 500 is the likely real outcome and is a defect.
rationale: The create action's rescue clause is narrow (RecordInvalid only); any ArgumentError from enum assignment escapes it, and product_type is a field integrations set from external strings.

title: XSS payload in product name and variant name is sanitized
preconditions: Family uuid bound to {{familyUuid}}; user has product create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /products with an img onerror payload in name and a script tag in the variant name
2. Assert status below 500
3. Assert neither the response nor the stored product_qualities row contains executable markup
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. sanitize_object recurses through nested hashes and arrays, so both the top-level name and variants[0].name are passed through strip_html_tags_except_mentions before the controller runs.
rationale: Variants arrive as an array of hashes, which is the case most likely to be missed by a sanitizer; proving the recursion covers nested params is worth its own test.

title: SQL injection payload in product_code must not execute
preconditions: Family uuid bound to {{familyUuid}}; note the current product count
steps: 1. POST /products with a UNION SELECT payload as the product_code
2. Assert the status is below 500
3. Call GET /products/search with a harmless query and confirm the products table still responds normally
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx and must not leak DB metadata. The value is stored as a literal string via a bound insert. Critically, Product.autocomplete_search interpolates the query into a raw where clause, so the stored value must also be safe to read back.
rationale: Product has a raw-SQL search scope that string-interpolates user input; a payload that is safe to write but explodes on read is a real and easily missed failure mode.

title: Create family under an existing category via parent_uuid
preconditions: An active L1 category exists in the workspace and its uuid is bound to {{categoryUuid}}
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with hierarchy_type family and parent_uuid {{categoryUuid}}
2. Assert HTTP 200
3. Assert the response parent linkage and capture the family uuid for product tests
expectedResult: HTTP 200. ParamsAuth#check_for_uuid rewrites parent_uuid to parent_id before the action runs, the controller resolves ProductCategory.active.find_by(id:, company_id: workspace), and the saved row has hierarchy_type=1 with ancestry set to the parent id.
rationale: This is the uuid-to-id decode contract plus the ancestry link in one call; if either breaks, every product created afterwards is orphaned from its L1.

title: Reject family create when parent_uuid points to a non-existent category
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with hierarchy_type family and a syntactically valid but unknown parent uuid
2. Assert HTTP 422 and error code 101
3. Assert no orphan family row was created
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'. ProductCategory.active.find_by(id:, company_id: Current.workspace.id) returns nil and the controller exits before build_product_category. No DB write.
rationale: The non-existent-parent and cross-tenant-parent cases collapse into the same 101 because the lookup is company-scoped; that is exactly the behaviour to pin so tenant isolation cannot silently regress into a 404.

title: Garbage parent_uuid that decodes to nil must not 500
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with parent_uuid set to a non-base64 junk string
2. Assert the status is below 500 and the body is JSON
3. Assert no family row was created
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. EncryptDecrypt.decode_data returns nil for undecodable input, so parent_id becomes nil and the create proceeds as a rootless family - or returns 422. Either is acceptable; a 500 or a silently rooted family the UI cannot place is a defect.
rationale: decode_data swallowing bad input into nil is a real trap: a mistyped uuid stops being 'not found' and becomes 'no parent at all'.

title: Reject family create with blank name under a valid parent
preconditions: An active L1 category exists and its uuid is bound to {{categoryUuid}}
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with a valid parent_uuid and an empty name
2. Assert HTTP 422 and error code 2
3. Assert the parent's children count is unchanged
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters'. The parent lookup succeeds first, then the blank-name guard fires; no child row is added under {{categoryUuid}}.
rationale: Order matters here - parent resolution runs before the blank check, so this proves a valid parent cannot mask a missing name and produce a partially built subtree.

title: Duplicate family name under the same parent
preconditions: A family named QA_Platform_DupFamily already exists under {{categoryUuid}}
steps: 1. Create a family named QA_Platform_DupFamily under {{categoryUuid}}
2. POST the identical payload a second time
3. Compare the two responses and count sibling rows
expectedResult: Must not 5xx. Sibling-name uniqueness lives in ProductCategory#validate_sibling_uniqueness which only runs when material_codification is enabled. With it off, the second call returns HTTP 200 and creates a duplicate sibling; with it on, HTTP 422 error.code 15.
rationale: A uniqueness rule that is config-gated is the highest-risk kind - the same request is legal on one tenant and illegal on another.

title: Family with hierarchy_type family but no parent creates a rootless family
preconditions: Authenticated buyer session with product_category create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /product_categories with hierarchy_type family and no parent_uuid at all
2. Record the HTTP status and the created row's ancestry
3. Query GET /product_categories and check whether the new family is reachable
expectedResult: Must not 5xx. The controller only validates the parent when parent_id.present?, so this returns HTTP 200 and persists hierarchy_type=1 with ancestry=NULL. The row is invisible to the index action and to all_children_of, i.e. orphan master data.
rationale: Nothing in the model requires a family to have a parent; proving the orphan is creatable and unreachable is the kind of silent data-quality bug that surfaces months later.

title: Create purchase team with name and team_type
preconditions: Authenticated buyer with team create_record permission; workspace resolved
steps: 1. POST /teams with name QA_Platform_Team_{{stamp}} and team_type purchase
2. Assert HTTP 200 and the rendered team partial
3. Capture the team uuid for the add-member cases
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with the team partial. New teams row: company_id=Current.workspace.id, status=1 (active, hard-set), team_type=0 (purchase). If the caller is neither super_admin nor a Procol employee, a TeamMember row is also created for the caller with role=member.
rationale: The implicit self-enrolment as a member for non-super-admin creators is an easy-to-miss side effect; verifying it prevents 'I created a team but cannot see it' regressions.

title: Reject team create when name is missing
preconditions: Authenticated buyer with team create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /teams with only team_type
2. Assert HTTP 422 and error code 2
3. Assert no teams row was created
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2 'Insufficient parameters' from the name.blank? || company_id.blank? guard, which runs before Pundit authorize. No DB write.
rationale: The guard runs before authorize team, so an unauthorized caller with a missing name gets 2 rather than 455 - that ordering is part of the contract and clients branch on the code.

title: Reject team create when name is whitespace only
preconditions: Authenticated buyer with team create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /teams with a whitespace-only name
2. Assert HTTP 422 and error code 2
3. Confirm no whitespace-named team appears in GET /teams/get_all
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 2. Rails blank? catches the whitespace-only string. Team has no model-level name presence validation at all, so this controller guard is the sole protection against nameless teams.
rationale: Team.name has neither a NOT NULL constraint nor a presence validation; the controller check is the only thing standing between a fat-fingered request and an unnamed team in every picker.

title: Invalid team_type enum must not 500
preconditions: Authenticated buyer with team create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /teams with team_type set to procurement
2. Assert the status is below 500 and the body is JSON
3. Assert no team was created
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. The controller does team.team_type = team_type with no validation; the enum is {purchase, quality_check, finance, logistics, payment, customer_support, zonal_purchase, planner, auction, it_support, vendor_management, process_validator, viewer}, so 'procurement' raises ArgumentError with no rescue.
rationale: 'procurement' is the most plausible wrong value a caller would guess for a procurement platform, making this the highest-probability real-world 500 on the endpoint.

title: Reject team create with a product category from another company
preconditions: A product category uuid that belongs to a different company is available; caller has team create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /teams with product_category_uuids containing a foreign category
2. Assert HTTP 422 and error code 101
3. Assert no team was created and no cross-tenant category id was stored
expectedResult: HTTP 422 with error.code 101 'You are not allowed to perform this action'. check_for_uuid rewrites product_category_uuids to product_category_ids, then validate_product_categories fails for ids outside [company_id]. No teams row created.
rationale: teams.product_category_ids is a plain integer array with a GIN index and no foreign key, so tenant isolation is enforced purely by validate_product_categories.

title: XSS and unicode in team name are handled safely
preconditions: Authenticated buyer with team create_record permission
steps: 1. POST /teams with a name mixing a script tag, Devanagari text and an emoji
2. Assert status below 500
3. Assert the returned team name has no script markup but retains the unicode characters
expectedResult: Must not return 5xx. sanitize_input_params strips the HTML tags before the action, so the team persists with the script markup removed while the Devanagari and emoji characters survive intact.
rationale: Combining sanitization and unicode in one payload catches the common bug where an over-aggressive sanitizer or a latin1 column mangles multibyte text while stripping tags.

title: QA_Platform_add_dispatch_must_not_500_on_missing_delivery_trackings
preconditions: a vendor-side caller
steps: 1. POST /delivery/add_dispatch_details with only shipment_info and no delivery_trackings key.
2. Assert a clean 4xx rather than an unhandled exception, and that no DeliveryTracking row is created.
expectedResult: Must be a 4xx with no DB write. Today Api::DeliveryTrackingsController#add_dispatch_details calls delivery_trackings.pluck('order_id') immediately after sanitize_params, so a missing key raises NoMethodError on nil - i.e. a 500 is the current behaviour and the guard is missing.
rationale: The dispatch endpoint has no presence validation at all before dereferencing the array; that is both a crash and a missing-validation finding on the goods-movement surface.

title: QA_Platform_add_dispatch_empty_array_passes_authorization_vacuously
preconditions: a vendor-side caller
steps: 1. POST /delivery/add_dispatch_details with delivery_trackings set to an empty array.
2. Assert no DeliveryTracking or Note row is created and record the status code.
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with an empty dispatches array and zero rows written: is_authorized([], false) compares 0 == 0 and passes vacuously, then the loop body never executes. No 5xx, no side effect.
rationale: An authorization check implemented as a count comparison returns true for an empty input set; harmless here, but it is exactly the shape of check that fails open when the id list is partially filtered.

title: QA_Platform_add_dispatch_rejects_unowned_order
preconditions: a vendor-side caller
steps: 1. POST /delivery/add_dispatch_details with a delivery_trackings entry whose order_id does not resolve to an order the caller sells.
2. Assert 101 and that no dispatch or invoice number is recorded.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 101; 'QA_Platform_...'.to_i is 0 so Order.where(id: 0, seller_company_id: Current.allowed_companies).size is 0 != 1 and is_authorized returns false before the transaction opens.
rationale: Dispatch records drive GRN and payment; a vendor being able to post dispatches against an order they do not own would let them invoice for goods they never shipped.

title: QA_Platform_add_dispatch_quantity_abuse_refused_before_write
preconditions: a vendor-side caller
steps: 1. POST /delivery/add_dispatch_details with a negative dispatched_quantity and an oversized one, against an order_id the caller does not own.
2. Assert the authorization refusal fires before any quantity is persisted.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 101 (unowned order) before add_delivery_info runs; no DeliveryTracking row with a negative or over-ordered quantity is created. If ownership ever passes, add_delivery_info must return false and yield error.code 534 instead of saving.
rationale: Negative and over-ordered dispatch quantities corrupt the dispatched-vs-ordered reconciliation used for payment; the test documents that ownership is checked first and that quantity validation is the next required gate.

title: QA_Platform_add_dispatch_ignores_unpermitted_status_param
preconditions: a vendor-side caller
steps: 1. POST /delivery/add_dispatch_details with extra top-level keys (status, buyer_company_id) alongside an unowned order_id.
2. Assert refusal and that the unpermitted keys are dropped by the strong-parameters filter.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 101; sanitize_params permits only shipment_info(dispatch_date, delivery_date, truck_number, driver_name, driver_contact_number) and delivery_trackings(order_id, dispatched_products(order_item_id, dispatched_quantity, invoice_number)), so status and buyer_company_id are discarded.
rationale: Mass-assignment through a dispatch payload is how a vendor could try to flip delivery state or re-point an order at another company; the permit list is the control.

title: QA_Platform_dispatch_read_blocks_foreign_order_ids
preconditions: a vendor-side caller who is neither buyer nor seller on {{orderUuid}}
steps: 1. GET /delivery/all?ids[]={{orderUuid}}.
2. Assert refusal and that no dispatch, truck or driver detail is returned.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 101 from is_authorized(order_ids, true), which requires all ids to belong to the caller's allowed companies as either buyer or seller.
rationale: Dispatch payloads contain driver names and contact numbers - personal data - alongside quantities, so the read side needs the same tenant proof as the write side.

title: QA_Platform_get_order_details_rejects_non_array_ids
preconditions: a caller who can read purchase orders in the current workspace
steps: 1. GET /orders/get_order_details?ids=QA_Platform_{{stamp}} passing a scalar instead of an array.
2. Assert the invalid-parameters refusal.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 888 (Invalid Parameters) from `render_error_json(888) unless order_ids.is_a?(Array)`.
rationale: The action pluck/maps over ids immediately after this guard; without it a scalar becomes a NoMethodError 500.

title: QA_Platform_get_order_details_blocks_cross_tenant_ids
preconditions: a caller whose workspace is neither the buyer nor the seller on {{orderUuid}}
steps: 1. GET /orders/get_order_details?ids[]={{orderUuid}} with an order the caller has no stake in.
2. Assert refusal and that no order item, price or dispatched quantity is returned.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 101; the action requires buyer_orders.size == ids.size OR seller_orders.size == ids.size against Current.allowed_companies, so a foreign id yields 0 matches and is refused.
rationale: PO line items carry negotiated unit prices; the all-or-nothing size comparison is the only tenant check here, and it also blocks id-mixing attacks where one owned id smuggles a foreign one.

title: QA_Platform_po_dms_attachments_rejects_unknown_invoice
preconditions: a caller who can read purchase orders in the current workspace
steps: 1. GET /orders/po_dms_attachments?invoice_no=QA_Platform_{{stamp}}.
2. Assert the no-order refusal instead of an empty media-log list.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 50 (No order found); the query is scoped to buyer_company_id = Current.workspace.id and where.not(status: :in_active).
rationale: DMS attachments are the signed PO documents; returning 200 with an empty list on an unknown invoice would hide misconfigured DMS pushes.

title: QA_Platform_order_show_by_uuid_documents_invoice_lookup_contract
preconditions: a caller who can read purchase orders in the current workspace
steps: 1. GET /orders/{{orderUuid}}.
2. Record whether the order is resolved, since the action matches params[:id] against invoice_no.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 50 (No order found) is the expected outcome: ParamsAuth#check_for_uuid decodes the uuid into a numeric id, but Api::OrdersController#show queries Order.where(invoice_no: params[:id]) and invoice_no is a 6-char SecureRandom hex string, so a numeric id cannot match. Must never 5xx.
rationale: A show endpoint that can never resolve by uuid is a real contract defect worth pinning: clients silently fall back to the index endpoint and nobody notices until PO detail pages break.

title: QA_Platform_po_index_survives_malformed_filters_json
preconditions: a caller who holds the po read_record permission
steps: 1. GET /purchase_orders with a filters parameter containing broken JSON.
2. Assert a 200 with unfiltered-but-tenant-scoped data and no stack trace.
expectedResult: HTTP 200: CommonFunctions.parse_filters rescues the JSON::ParserError and returns nil, and OrdersControllerFilterHelper#create_filter_params_for_orders rescues StandardError, so the request degrades to an unfiltered but workspace-scoped list; no 500.
rationale: Filter payloads are user-controlled JSON pasted from the UI; the two independent rescues must both hold or the whole PO page 500s for one bad saved view.

title: QA_Platform_po_index_survives_invalid_status_enum_filter
preconditions: a caller who holds the po read_record permission
steps: 1. GET /purchase_orders with a filters payload whose po_status value is not a purchase_order_status enum member.
2. Assert the API either returns an empty/unfiltered 200 or a clean 4xx, never a 500.
expectedResult: No 5xx. Order.enum purchase_order_status is {not_requested:0, requested:1, generated:2, declined:3}; the has_scope :po_status array scope must handle the unknown member as an empty result set (HTTP 200 with zero orders) rather than raising ArgumentError.
rationale: Enum filters coming from a stale front-end build are a common source of production 500s, and this scope is applied via has_scope with no whitelist.

title: QA_Platform_purchase_orders_index_read
preconditions: a caller who holds the po read_record permission
steps: 1. GET /purchase_orders?page=1.
2. Assert HTTP 200 and that every returned order belongs to the caller's workspace with stats fields present.
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with data, total_pages, number_of_purchase_orders, number_of_success_po, number_of_failed_po and po_dms_enabled; PurchaseOrders::SearchQueryPo forces buyer_company_id = Current.workspace.id and excludes in_active.
rationale: This is the PO list every buyer lands on; the workspace clause inside the query object is the tenant boundary for all PO data.

title: QA_Platform_po_page_stats_read
preconditions: a caller who holds the po read_record permission
steps: 1. GET /purchase_orders/po_page_stats.
2. Assert HTTP 200 and that the counters are integers consistent with the index response.
expectedResult: HTTP 200 with total_line_items_procured, avg_time_cycle and the five purchase_order_status counters (not_requested/requested/generated/declined) computed by group(:purchase_order_status).count.
rationale: These counters are what procurement leadership reports on; a silent enum rename would zero them out without any error surfacing.

title: QA_Platform_create_po_rejects_unresolvable_contract
preconditions: a caller who holds the po read_record permission (OrderPolicy#create_po? maps to index?)
steps: 1. POST /orders/QA_Platform_{{stamp}}/create_po with a pr_to_po request_type and one line item.
2. Assert the contract-not-found refusal and that no Order/PO row and no budget call are made.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 476 (Contract not found): ParamsAuth turns the contract_uuid path segment into contract_id = nil, so Order.find_by(id: nil, buyer_company_id: workspace) is nil and the guard returns before handle_budget_integration and Contracts::ContractConsumptionService.
rationale: Create_po is the single most side-effectful endpoint in this flow; proving it dies on the contract lookup with an unresolvable uuid is the only safe way to exercise it.

title: QA_Platform_po_stats_schema_rejects_missing_line_item
preconditions: a caller who holds the po read_record permission
steps: 1. GET /orders/po_stats_schema with no event_group_line_item_id.
2. Assert the line-item-not-found refusal.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 808 (Line item not found); EventGroupLineItem.not_in_active.find_by(id: nil) is nil so the cache is never populated.
rationale: The response is cached for a day keyed off the line item; a missing-id path that fell through would poison the cache with an empty schema.

title: QA_Platform_po_stats_schema_rejects_foreign_line_item
preconditions: a caller who holds the po read_record permission but whose workspace does NOT own {{eventGroupUuid}}
steps: 1. GET /orders/po_stats_schema?event_group_line_item_uuid={{eventGroupUuid}} using an identifier from another tenant.
2. Assert no historic price data is returned.
expectedResult: HTTP 422: error.code 808 when the id does not resolve, or 455 from authorize egli.event_group, :show? when it resolves to another workspace's event group; historic PO prices are never disclosed.
rationale: This endpoint exposes historic award prices per product; the second pundit check on the event group is the cross-tenant guard and it must be asserted, not trusted.

title: QA_Platform_update_po_status_rejects_unknown_agribid_id
preconditions: an integration-style caller reaching the SAP callback (OrderPolicy#update_purchase_order_status? returns true for everyone)
steps: 1. POST /orders/update_po_status with a fabricated agribid_id, status success and a PO number.
2. Assert the request-not-found refusal and that no Order row anywhere changes purchase_order_status.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 4 (Request not found) because Order.where(invoice_no: params['agribid_id']).last is nil; purchase_order_status, po_number and po_details are untouched and the po-generated after_commit hooks (DMS upload, flexi worker) never fire.
rationale: This is the SAP-facing endpoint whose policy method returns true unconditionally, so the invoice lookup is the ONLY thing preventing an arbitrary caller from marking POs as generated.

title: QA_Platform_update_po_status_handles_unknown_status_value
preconditions: an integration-style caller reaching the SAP callback
steps: 1. POST /orders/update_po_status with a fabricated agribid_id and a status outside success/error/warning.
2. Assert no crash and no state change.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 4 (order not found). Note for the report: had the order existed, none of the success/error/warning branches would match, yet order.save would still persist the attacker-supplied po_details - the lookup is the only protection. No 5xx.
rationale: The action has no status whitelist and saves unconditionally; documenting that gap while staying on a non-existent order is the safe way to file it.

title: QA_Platform_update_po_rejects_missing_po_number
preconditions: a caller who is NOT a super_admin and is not a Procol employee (OrderPolicy#update_po? requires is_procol_employee?)
steps: 1. POST /orders/update_po with invoice_no only.
2. Assert the call is refused either by the policy or by the param guard, and that no PO number is written.
expectedResult: HTTP 422: error.code 455 for a non-Procol-employee caller (authorize Order runs first), or error.code 2 (Insufficient parameters) for a permitted caller since po_number is blank. purchase_order_status is never set to generated and upload_attachments_to_po_dms is not invoked.
rationale: update_po force-marks an order as generated and triggers the DMS upload; both the pundit gate and the param gate must be proven to fire before that.

title: QA_Platform_update_po_rejects_unknown_invoice_no
preconditions: a caller who is NOT a super_admin and is not a Procol employee
steps: 1. POST /orders/update_po with a fabricated invoice_no and a PO number.
2. Assert refusal and that no order is marked generated.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 455 (policy) or 50 (No order found); po_details is not blanked and purchase_order_status stays as-is.
rationale: Note this action is NOT scoped to Current.workspace - it finds by invoice_no globally - so the is_procol_employee? policy is the entire tenant control and deserves a standing negative test.

title: QA_Platform_retry_po_rejects_blank_invoice_no
preconditions: a caller who can act on purchase orders in the current workspace
steps: 1. PATCH /orders/retry_po with a po_details object but no invoice_no.
2. Assert refusal before any contract or PO generation worker is queued.
expectedResult: HTTP 422 error.code 2; the invoice_no.blank? guard runs before the Order lookup, so retry_count is not incremented and neither run_contract_generator_worker nor generate_purchase_order is called.
rationale: Retry re-emits a PO to the ERP; a blank identifier reaching the lookup is how duplicate POs get generated for the wrong vendor.

title: QA_Platform_retry_po_rejects_unknown_proposal
